explanation: Faithfully states the Bleicher–Erdős lower bound R(N) ≥ (N/log N)∏_{3≤i≤k} log_i N, valid for k ≥ 4 with log_k N ≥ k. R(N) is the largest A ⊆ [1,N] with all subset reciprocal sums distinct, encoded as InjOn on the powerset. Real.log takes absolute values, but the hypothesis log_k N ≥ k ≥ 4 effectively forces a genuine chain of large iterates, so I see no spurious small-N instances.
